lede: A Catholic publishing house in St. Louis, Missouri, founded in 2014 by Dr. Ronda Chervin and Dr. Sebastian Mahfood, OP, to promote the Catholic spiritual journey by publishing books that serve it.
body:
En Route operates as a traditional publisher on a print-on-demand model. Books are produced as they are ordered, so there are no warehousing costs and no large upfront print runs. That lets the house stay small, take on work a larger press would not, and keep going: nearly 700 titles since the founding, and a catalog that spans theology, philosophy, spirituality, poetry, literature, biography, business, science, and children's books.

As a traditional publisher, En Route assumes the cost of preparing a book for publication. Authors receive a 10 percent royalty on retail sales and may buy copies at a 40 percent discount. The model reflects a commitment to mission over scale: by removing the financial burden of large print runs, the house can publish scholars, clergy, poets, and new authors on the merit of the work.

In 2016 En Route partnered with WCAT Radio, which now hosts more than a hundred programs and thousands of podcast episodes and gives every author a place to be heard. Eligible paperbacks print on groundwood paper for a richer, more tactile read.

We are grateful to our authors, readers, and listeners for helping us continue this mission of sharing the richness of the Catholic intellectual and spiritual tradition.

founders.bio: Dr. Ronda Chervin co-founded En Route in 2014. A philosopher, convert, widow, and author of dozens of books on the spiritual life, she gives several of her titles away free through the house, including The Last Fling, Spiritual Friendship, and God Alone. Free downloads →

founders.name: Sebastian Mahfood, OP
founders.bio:
Dr. Sebastian Mahfood, OP, co-founded En Route Books and Media in 2014 with Dr. Ronda Chervin and is its president, and the producer of WCAT Radio. A Lay Dominican, he has spent his career in Catholic higher education and distance learning, which is where the house's instinct for reaching readers wherever they are comes from.
